title: Electrical Power Safety: De-Energize, Lock Out, Tag
summary: Contact with live circuits causes shock, burns, falls, and electrocution, even for experienced electricians. This talk covers verifying de-energization, lockout devices, and tags.
talking_points: Make sure circuits are de-energized before any work on or near them. Test with an AC voltage detector to confirm.
Use lockout devices so the circuit cannot be turned back on.
Put a tag on the locked circuit to warn others not to energize it.
Never assume a labeled breaker is off. Others, including the utility, may energize a circuit without your knowledge.
Treat equipment marked high-voltage as dangerous even when disconnected. It can store lethal energy.
site_hazards_to_check: Circuits worked on without a voltage test to confirm they are dead
Breakers or disconnects labeled but not locked out
Missing warning tags on locked-out equipment
High-voltage equipment assumed safe because it is unplugged
Other crews or utility workers able to energize the same circuit
discussion_questions: How do you confirm a circuit is really dead before you touch it?
Who else could energize this circuit while we are working on it?
Why can high-voltage equipment still hurt you after it is disconnected?

flags: OSHA mapping verified accurate: 1926.416 (general requirements - de-energize/protect employees) and 1926.417 (lockout and tagging of circuits). Verify-dead-with-a-tester, lockout devices, warning tags, do not trust labels, treat disconnected high-voltage equipment as still able to store lethal energy - all consistent with the standard. No tolerance issues.
